title: Levántate, búscalo, no te rindas
goal: a usar los phrasal verbs más frecuentes y a poner la fuerza en la partícula

ex.t: I get up early to go for a walk.
ex.es: Me levanto temprano para ir a caminar.

ex.t: I'm looking for my reading glasses.
ex.es: Estoy buscando las gafas de leer.

ex.t: I look after my grandson on Fridays.
ex.es: Cuido a mi nieto los viernes.

ex.t: Don't give up! Your English is great.
ex.es: ¡No te rindas! Tu inglés es estupendo.

ex.t: I found out the news on WhatsApp.
ex.es: Me enteré de la noticia por WhatsApp.

ex.t: Can you pick me up at the station?
Please turn off your phone in the theatre.
ex.es: Por favor, apague el móvil en el teatro.

ex.t: I'm looking forward to seeing my family.
ex.es: Tengo muchas ganas de ver a mi familia.

vocab.note: Detrás va un nombre o -ing: look forward to seeing.

pron.title: La fuerza va en la partícula
pron.tip: En los phrasal verbs, la palabra pequeña suele llevar la fuerza: get UP, give UP, find OUT, pick it UP, turn it OFF. Si la dices floja, cuesta entenderte.

exercises.q: What time do you usually ___ on Sundays?
I'm ___ my keys. Have you seen them?
Your phone is ringing in the cinema! Turn ___!
exercises.why: Con pronombre, en medio: turn it off.
Tener ganas de = look forward to.

exercises.q: How did you find ___ about the wedding?
We've run out ___ bread. Can you buy some?
exercises.es: Nos hemos quedado sin pan. ¿Puedes comprar?

exercises.q: My husband gave ___ chocolate for a month. It didn't last!
exercises.es: Mi marido dejó el chocolate un mes. ¡No le duró!

exercises.q: Can you pick up my grandson at five?
answer: Can you pick him up at five?
exercises.why: Pick up se separa: pick him up.

exercises.q: Could you look after the plants?
exercises.why: Look after no se separa: look after them.

exercises.q: I'm looking after a nice restaurant near here.
exercises.why: Buscar = look for. Look after = cuidar.

exercises.q: We set up at six to avoid the traffic.

answer: I'm really looking forward to seeing you.
I'm looking forward to seeing you.
I am really looking forward to seeing you.
I am looking forward to seeing you.

exercises.context: Tu amiga quiere dejar las clases de inglés porque le cuesta. La animas.
options: Don't give up! You're doing so well.
Don't give it! You're doing so well.
Don't get up! You're doing so well.
exercises.answer: Don't give up! You're doing so well.
exercises.why: No te rindas = Don't give up.

exercises.answer: I'll pick you up at the airport

exercises.why: Phrasal verbs del día a día.

exercises.t: Don't give up! Pick it up again tomorrow.
exercises.es: ¡No te rindas! Vuelve a cogerlo mañana.

dialog.title: La mañana de la vuelta
dialog.setting: En el hotel de Londres, la última mañana; Yolanda busca sus cosas y Emma la llama

lines.t: Morning! Have you got up yet?
Yes, but I'm looking for my passport!
Don't panic. Did you look in your handbag?
lines.es: Que no cunda el pánico. ¿Has mirado en el bolso?

lines.t: Here it is! Sorry, I've run out of patience this morning.
lines.es: ¡Aquí está! Perdona, esta mañana se me ha acabado la paciencia.

lines.t: Ha ha! What time are you setting off?
At ten. Can you pick me up?
Of course. I'll take you to St Pancras.
lines.es: Claro. Te llevo a St Pancras.

lines.t: Thank you! I'll turn off the heating and go down.

realLife.t: Could you pick me up at the station?
realLife.context: Para pedirle a tu hijo o a una amiga que vaya a buscarte

summary: Verbo + partícula = significado nuevo: look for, look after, give up, find out
Separables con pronombre en medio: turn it off, pick me up
No separables: look for it, look after them
La fuerza va en la partícula: give UP, find OUT
